Mr. 1, 21.''}}* And he vvent dovvne into Capharnaum a citie of Galilee: and there he taught them on the Sabboths. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=32}} And they vvere a{{ls}}tonied at his doctrine: becau{{ls}}e his talke vvas in povver. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=33}} And in the {{ls}}ynagogue there vvas a man hauing an vncleane Diuel, and he cried out vvith a loud voice, {{verse|chapter=4|verse=34}} {{ls}}aying, Let be, vvhat to vs and thee {{sc|Iesvs}} of Nazareth? art thou come to de{{ls}}troy vs? I know thee vvho thou art, ''the {{sc|Sainct}} of God''. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=35}} And {{sc|Iesvs}} rebuked him, {{ls}}aying, Hold thy peace, & goe out of him. And vvhen the Deuil had throvven him into the middes, he vvent out of him, and hurted him nothing. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=36}} And there came feare vpon al, and they talked together one vvith an other, {{ls}}aying, VVhat vvord is this, that in povver and vertue he commaundeth the vncleane {{ls}}pirits, and they goe out? {{verse|chapter=4|verse=37}} And the fame of him vvas publi{{ls}}hed into euery place of the countrie.

{{verse|chapter=4|verse=38}} {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mat. 8, 14. Mr. 1, 30.''}}* And {{sc|Iesvs}} ri{{ls}}ing vp out of the {{ls}}ynagogue, entred into Simons hou{{ls}}e. {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Go{{ls}}pel vpon Thur{{ls}}day in the 3. vveeke of Lent. And vpon Saturday in Vvhit{{ls}}onvveeke.}}And {{sup|‖}} Simons vviues mother vvas holden with a great feuer: and they be{{ls}}ought him for her. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=39}} And {{ls}}tanding ouer her, he commaunded the feuer, and it left her. And incontinent ri{{ls}}ing, {{ls}}he mini{{ls}}tred to them. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=40}} And vvhen the {{ls}}unne vvas dovvne, al that had di{{ls}}ea{{ls}}ed of {{ls}}undrie maladies, brought them to him. But he impo{{ls}}ing hands vpon euery one, cured them. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=41}} And Deuils vvent out from many, crying and {{ls}}aying, That thou art the {{ls}}onne of God. And rebuking them he {{ls}}uffred them not to {{ls}}peake, that they knevv he vvas Chri{{ls}}t.

{{verse|chapter=4|verse=42}} And vvhen it vvas day, going forth he vvent into a de{{ls}}ert place: and the multitudes {{ls}}ought him, and came euen vnto him: and they held him that he {{ls}}hould not depart from them. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=43}} To vvhom he {{ls}}aid, That to other cities al{{ls}}o mu{{ls}}t I euangelize the kingdom of God: becau{{ls}}e therfore I vvas {{ls}}ent. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=44}} And he vvas preaching in the {{ls}}ynagogs of Galilee.⊣
